pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Holy Trinity CofE Primary School
Our 2-form entry Church of England school sits in the heart of the community surrounding South Park Gardens, Wimbledon. We are proud of our close links with Holy Trinity Church and our partnership with The Priory C of E Primary School.
At Holy Trinity, through our deeply Christian, theologically-rooted vision, we aim to help children understand that they are uniquely created by God, and are loved and valued for who they are. We support each child to flourish and to achieve their full potential by providing the best possible education, firmly rooted in Christian values. We encourage children to develop a spirit of enquiry, as well as perseverance and a capacity to question, listen and discuss things reasonably with others and to work independently.
We seek to be outward looking so that we can have a positive impact on our community – locally, nationally and internationally.
At Holy Trinity, we welcome and encourage active interest and participation in children’s education and the life of the school. We believe that working together with parents/carers and the wider community provides the best support for our children.
We hope that you will find all the information that you will need to help you here. If you do need any further information, or would like to arrange a visit to our school, please email headteacher@holytrinity.merton.sch.uk
If you have any questions or queries please contact me on 0208542 1591, or via email headteacher@holytrinity.merton.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - Our Faith
pageCache.text:
Our Faith
Our Faith
At Holy Trinity Church of England Primary School we are proud of our strong Christian ethos, which is at the heart of all that we do. We want all of our school community to flourish and live life in all its fullness (John 10:10). We want children and adults to start, or strengthen, their spiritual journey, during their time at Holy Trinity. Our Christian vision is to ensure that we are all Growing together as Children of God.
We want our pupils to grow in confidence, independence, resilience and knowledge, so that all achieve their full potential, and develop a life-long love of learning.
We work together with families, community and the church to model positive relationships, supporting each other, and acknowledging that we are stronger when we work together.
We are growing together as children of God, strengthening our faith, secure in the knowledge that we are unique, loved and cherished.
At the heart of our Christian vision is the story of Jesus healing the paralysed man, from Matthew 9:1-8. This healing reminds us of the importance of Jesus' teaching on forgiveness, friendship, care for others and trust - these are all at the centre of our school.
The Christian values of love, thankfulness and forgiveness underpin our life at Holy Trinity.
Worship and prayer are central to the life of our school. Our daily act of Christian worship helps us to focus on God, right at the start of the day. Our worship seeks to be inclusive, invitational and inspirational, through bible stories, singing praises to God and praying. Our termly Eucharist offers an opportunity, for those who wish to, to share bread and wine in order to remember the death of Jesus onthe cross. The school regularly visits Holy Trinity Church for services, which are often led by our Growing Together in Spirit team.
Prayers spaces in the school entrance and in classrooms encourage prayer throughout the day.
Our Spirituality Policy explains how spirituality is fostered throughout our school, in learning, in worship and in our relationships. We aim to:
1) Provide opportunities for pupils to encounter the Christian faith and reflect on its significance.
2) Enable pupils and staff to develop their own spirituality through the believing (we feel it), thinking (we think it) and living (we live it) lenses.
3) Encourage pupils to engage thoughtfully with questions of meaning, truth and values.
4) Foster respect, empathy and compassion for others, regardless of belief.
5) Equip pupils to make reasoned and informed responses to moral and ethical issues.
To help us all Grow together as children of God we follow our Growing Together Rules, based on Matthew 7:12, "Treat others as you want then to treat you."
Our most recent SIAMS (Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools) inspection in July 2026, highlighted many notable strengths, and confirmed that we are living up to our foundation as a Church school and are enabling pupils and adults to flourish.
Do read our SIAMS report, which we are so proud of.
Our SIAMS Self-Evaluation Form, Collective Worship, Spirituality and Religious Education Policies can be accessed below. Our Junior Leadership Team have been working on the Race and Equality Charter, which can be accessed below.
Be respectful
Be kind
Be safe
Be ready

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - Holy Trinity Church
pageCache.text:
Our School
Holy Trinity Church
We are proud to be in the parish of Holy Trinity Church. Our school has a strong Christian ethos. There is regular worship, often led by clergy from the parish. The parish appoints governors to the governing body of the school. Children often visit church for acts of worship or for other visits.
The admissions policies of the school allocates half of places as 'foundation places', for the children of families who worship regularly in Christian churches. Amongst these, priority goes to those who worship in one of the three churches in Merton Priory parish.
We know that it is a privilege to be able to encourage children to grow in love for God and respect for each other. Each year we celebrate the strong relationship between our church and schools on 'Schools Sunday' in the Autumn, when staff, governors, and pupils come to our Parish Eucharist and we pray for them and all they will do in the coming year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is an independently run business by two of the school Early Years Practitioners, Carol Sumner and Tina Panners.
The club runs from 7:45 - 8:45am each morning and provides children from Reception to Year 6 with a healthy breakfast (served until 8:00) and good quality social and learning activities.
It is very popular and so it is important that parents submit the booking form which is available from either Carol or Tina.
Important Information:
1) Children must be booked in to attend
2) Payment of £6 per session must be made in advance
3) Children must be signed in by an adult each morning
4) Breakfast is served until 8:00am
For further information and enquiries please contact Carol and Tina at tc@holytrinity.merton.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - RSE Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Teaching & Learning
RSE Curriculum
At Holy Trinity, good relationships are fundamental to our ethos and our success in being a happy, caring and safe school. Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is lifelong learning about relationships, emotions, looking after ourselves, different families, sex, sexuality and sexual health. Our RSE curriculum ensures that children are able to cherish themselves and others as unique and wonderfully made, keep themselves safe and able to form healthy relationships where they respect and afford dignity to others. It will provide pupils with age-appropriate knowledge (see curriculum overview for further information) that will enable them to navigate a world in which many will try to tell them how to behave, what to do and what to think. This is a responsibility that is shared between parents/carers and school.
At Holy Trinity, we follow the Christopher Winters Project: Teaching RSE with Confidence in Primary Schools. This provides a clear progression of age-appropriate knowledge and skills from foundation through to year 6. Clear lesson plans and resources give the teachers confidence to address what we recognise can be a challenging area of the curriculum to deliver. The lessons are clearly mapped to follow the National Curriculum for science and DfE Statutory Guidance on Relationships Education, Relationship and Sex Education and Health Education. The majority of RSE will be delivered through PSHE and science lessons.
The RSE curriculum covers the following areas (progressing from Reception up to year 6):
● Family and friendship
● Growing and Caring for Ourselves
● Valuing differences and keeping safe
● Puberty, relationships and reproduction
Children will be confident to talk about their bodies, using correct terminology. They will be confident to talk about the changes their bodies go through as they grow and have a clear idea about positive and healthy relationships (including online relationships). The progressive scheme gradually builds up children’s knowledge and vocabulary, so that by the end of Year 6, children will have a clear understanding about the effects and purpose of puberty and reproduction (conception and pregnancy). The majority of progress will be assessed through class based discussion.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - Governors Capital Fund
pageCache.text:
Our School
Governors Capital Fund
Governors Captial Fund (£25 per child per term)
Holy Trinity is a Voluntary Aided school and as a result, we receive money to pay for staff and resources through the London Borough of Merton. However, as a VA school our capital projects are funded through the Southwark Diocese, with the exception of 10% of the cost of all capital work which is funded by the Governors.
We are fortunate to have a relatively new school building but now, six years after the majority of our expansion work was completed, things are inevitably needing to be fixed or updated. In the past we have worked with the Diocese to replace the boiler, repair drainage, install new fencing and repair our ventilation systems. Whilst these items are not glamourous they are nonetheless vital in providing a safe environment in which children can learn. We also fund projects which have a more visible impact on children and their families including dyslexia-friendly and sensory equipment as well as Mindfulness training for pupils.
Like other VA schools we ask parents to contribute to the Governors Subscription Fund which we use to pay our 10% contribution to the Diocese (approximately £8000 per year) and to provide additional money for school improvement. Our only source of income to the Governors Fund is parental contributions.
Payments are collected through ParentMail on a termly basis.
We wish to reiterate that these are voluntary payments and we are very aware that not all families are in a position to make these contributions, particularly those with more than one child at the school. We would be grateful for any contribution you feel able to make, however large or small, and if you have any questions with regard to making payments please speak with the team in the school office.
Thank you for all of your support.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holy Trinity CofE Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Teaching & Learning
Music
At Holy Trinity we want every child to flourish and be able to develop their God-give talents, skills and gifts. Holy Trinity's Music scheme of work aims to inspire our children and develop their confidence to experiment and create their own music as an important part of their entitlement to a broad and balanced curriculum. It is designed to empower all of our young learners, including those with SEND, to develop their ability, nurture their talent, express their individual interests, ideas and thoughts about the world, as well as learning about the rich heritage and culture of great musicians in the British Isles and beyond.
At Holy Trinity, music skills are taught, learned, embedded and built upon in each unit the children study and these skills are revisited and developed as they progress through primary school and beyond.
We support our children to reach the National Curriculum end of key stage attainment targets, whilst knowing how music both reflects and shapes our history and contributes to the culture, creativity and wealth of our nation.
